objects.description: Helper class providing CMake/CTest version information. It exposes static query functions for the major, minor, patch, and tweak numbers, as well as a combined human-readable version string. No instances are required or expected; all APIs are static. Construction, ownership, and lifecycle are therefore not applicable beyond normal C++ class semantics.

functions.name: cmVersion::GetMajorVersion
functions.description: Returns the major version number of CMake. Use to programmatically query CMake’s major version for feature gating or compatibility checks.
requirements: No documented preconditions or side effects.
Return value is an unsigned integer representing the major version component.

functions.name: cmVersion::GetMinorVersion
functions.description: Returns the minor version number of CMake. Use alongside the major version to determine specific version compatibility or to display version information.
requirements: No documented preconditions or side effects.
Return value is an unsigned integer representing the minor version component.

functions.name: cmVersion::GetPatchVersion
functions.description: Returns the patch version number of CMake. Useful for precise version checks and diagnostics.
requirements: No documented preconditions or side effects.
Return value is an unsigned integer representing the patch version component.

functions.name: cmVersion::GetTweakVersion
functions.description: Returns the tweak (build/extra) version number of CMake, if defined. Helpful for distinguishing builds that share the same major.minor.patch.
requirements: No documented preconditions or side effects.
Return value is an unsigned integer representing the tweak version component.

functions.name: cmVersion::GetCMakeVersion
functions.description: Returns the complete CMake version as a C-style, null-terminated string (e.g., "X.Y.Z" with an optional tweak). Intended for display or logging of the full version.
requirements: Caller must treat the returned string as read-only (const) and must not attempt to modify or free it.
No documented preconditions or side effects. The returned pointer is expected to remain valid per typical library version-string patterns, but exact lifetime is not documented in this header.
